notes: BETA 2.28.91. iRacing finally gets a track map: iRacing does not share where your car is, so PitWise now works it out from the car's heading and speed, closes the map when you cross the line after your first full lap, and from then on keeps the car dot glued to the track by lap distance. The racing line coach now works in iRacing too - it estimates how far left or right you are of your own line and, after a few consistent laps, tells you where you run wide or tight compared with your best lap. A tow or pit visit during the first lap no longer bends the map. Imola, Mount Panorama and Gilles Villeneuve now pick up their named corners in iRacing. Track map for every sim: rotate it in 90 degree steps and mirror it, saved per track. You can now edit corners yourself: click the track to mark a corner or a point of interest (straights too), name it, rename or delete it - your corners replace the automatic ones everywhere, and the engineer says your name for it exactly as you typed it, with the rest of the sentence in your language. Also in this beta: PitWise no longer runs out of Windows window handles at startup with a wheel or pedals plugged in (Error creating window handle), the engineer no longer announces your position every few seconds when cars swap places and there is a new switch for position calls, voice volume goes up to 200 percent (a few dB louder, not double), the list of questions you can ask after an answer is now optional, if the AI cannot be reached the engineer says so instead of answering something else, questions are no longer mistaken for pit commands, and in Le Mans Ultimate qualifying with ghosted cars the spotter stays quiet; spotter calls about cars around you are always spoken instantly without going through the AI. None of this has been tested on track yet - iRacing testers especially, please report how the map, the car dot and the line tips behave.
